newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia boosts coffee sales to U.S. and Canada.
newsitem.headline: Colombia boosts coffee sales to U.S. and Canada.

text.p: Colombia's coffee sales to the United States and Canada perked up 22.6 percent this year from sales in 1995, according to Jorge Cardenas, veteran leader of the National Growers' Federation.
He said sales to Japan were also sharply higher, totalling 1.15 million 60-kilo bags against 994,000 bags in 1995.
In the United States and Canada, 1996 sales totaled 2.83 million bags, up from 2.30 million in 1995, Cardenas said.
He attributed the growth in U.S. and Canadian sales, at least in part, to the success of the "100-percent Colombian" brands marketed by Kraft and Folgers.
Cardenas spoke in his annual address to the National Coffee Growers' Congress in Bogota where he said Colombia's coffee sales grew by 750,000 60-bags in 1996 over 1995.

The jump in sales to the United States and Canada accounted for tightnesss in supply for the European market, where Colombia's coffee sales fell 1.0 percent in 1996 to a total of 5.3 million bags, Cardenas said.
Europe remained, by far, the single most important market for Colombian coffee, however.
